  "hypotheses": [
    {
      "explanation":"household",
      "likelihood":"high",
      "reasoning":"A newly registered customer sharing a home address plausibly explains the address linkage. The passed identity check establishes that the customer holds both the payment credentials and account identity, although the address tenure does not qualify for the household exception."
    },
    {
      "explanation":"synthetic_identity",
      "likelihood":"low",
      "reasoning":"Address linkage initially raises a duplicated-identity concern, but there is no matching normalized email or multi-account device activity. The passed identity check further weakens this explanation."
    }

  "disposition":"clear",
  "citations":["R08","FP-2 §6.4(b)","FP-2 §6.6(b)","FP-2 §5.2","FP-2 §5.3(a)","FP-2 §6.3"],
  "next_check":"none",
  "memo":"R08 holds, making Linkage the only adverse family. The home-address household exception does not apply because the address was only recently registered. No other rule holds, and no earlier outcome settles the order. Under FP-2 §6.6(b), Linkage required id_check; that check passed. Every required check has therefore passed, so §5.3(a) mandates clear and prohibits further holding, declining, escalation or needs_check. Ordinary household sharing is the strongest benign explanation. Verification resolves the identity concern, not repayment intent. No further check is needed."
